title: Grammar: If/Whether Clauses, Embedded Questions, and Noun Clause Patterns
grammarTip:
Косвенные вопросы (Indirect / Embedded questions) — вопрос внутри предложения:

Прямой вопрос → Косвенный (порядок слов меняется!):
"Where is she?" → "Do you know WHERE SHE IS?" (не "where is she")
"What time does it start?" → "Could you tell me WHAT TIME IT STARTS?"
"Is he coming?" → "I wonder WHETHER/IF HE IS COMING."

⚠️ Главное правило: в косвенном вопросе порядок слов как в утверждении!
❌ "Can you tell me where IS the library?"
✅ "Can you tell me where THE LIBRARY IS?"

Вежливые формулы:
"Could you tell me...?" · "Do you know...?" · "I wonder..."
"I'd like to know..." · "Would you mind telling me...?"

grammarTable.subject: whether / if clause
grammarTable.example: "I wonder whether the story is accurate." / "She asked if the site was reliable."

grammarTable.subject: wh-word + embedded Q
grammarTable.example: "Tell me what you found." / "Do you know who wrote this article?"

grammarTable.subject: Question of whether
grammarTable.verb: the question of whether + S + V
grammarTable.example: "The question of whether AI should generate news is unresolved."

grammarTable.subject: Whether to + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "She couldn't decide whether to share the article or wait for verification."

grammarTable.subject: noun + wh-clause
grammarTable.example: "The issue of how news is monetised affects quality." / "The matter of who owns media matters."

grammarTable.subject: Not know / wonder / doubt + whether
grammarTable.example: "I doubt whether regulation can keep up with technology." / "She wonders whether she can trust the source."

rows.form: Both can introduce embedded yes/no questions after verbs
rows.example: "I wonder whether/if the report is accurate." (both are correct)

rows.form: Only "whether" after prepositions
rows.example: "The debate about whether social media is regulated fairly." ✅ NOT "about if"

rows.form: Only "whether" before "or not"
rows.example: "She can't decide whether or not to publish." ✅ NOT "if or not"

rows.form: Only "whether" as a subject noun clause
rows.example: "Whether the site is reliable remains unclear." ✅ NOT "If the site is reliable…"

rows.form: Only "whether" before to-infinitive
rows.example: "She didn't know whether to share the story." ✅ NOT "if to share"

rows.form: Direct question → Embedded question (no auxiliary inversion)
rows.example: "Where does misinformation come from?" → "I don't know where misinformation comes from."

rows.form: What is... → what ... is
rows.example: "What is the source?" → "Can you tell me what the source is?"

rows.form: Why did... → why ... did/does
rows.example: "Why did the story spread?" → "She wondered why the story spread so quickly."

rows.form: How do... → how ... do/does
rows.example: "How do algorithms work?" → "I want to understand how algorithms work."

rows.form: The question of whether + S + V
rows.example: "The question of whether social media should be regulated more strictly is politically contentious."

rows.form: The issue of how + S + V
rows.example: "The issue of how we fund quality journalism is urgent."

rows.form: The matter of who + S + V
rows.example: "The matter of who owns major news outlets affects what gets reported."

rows.form: The problem of what + S + V
rows.example: "The problem of what counts as reliable news is difficult to resolve."

grammarExtra.title: Useful Verbs for Embedded Questions in Academic Writing

rows.form: Wonder, ask, consider, debate, examine, investigate + wh-/whether
rows.example: "Researchers are examining whether filter bubbles reduce exposure to opposing views."

rows.form: Know, understand, explain, discover, find out + wh-/whether
rows.example: "She found out who was behind the disinformation campaign."

rows.form: Doubt, question, dispute + whether
rows.example: "Many doubt whether self-regulation by platforms is sufficient."

rows.form: Determine, decide, choose + whether to + infinitive
rows.example: "Editors must decide whether to publish unverified information during breaking news."

rows.form: ❌ I wonder where is she working.
rows.example: ✅ I wonder where she is working. (no inversion in embedded questions)

rows.form: ❌ She asked what did he say.
rows.example: ✅ She asked what he said. (no auxiliary inversion)

rows.form: ❌ The debate about if regulation is needed.
rows.example: ✅ The debate about whether regulation is needed. (use "whether" after prepositions)

rows.form: ❌ She couldn't decide if to publish.
rows.example: ✅ She couldn't decide whether to publish. (use "whether" before to-infinitive)

exercises.text: "The debate about ___ social media companies should be regulated is ongoing."
"I don't know ___ the article ___ (be) accurate." (= I don't know whether it's accurate)
exercises.hint: "Whether + S + V" — no inversion, present tense

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct embedded question form.
exercises.text: "Can you tell me ___ the information comes from?"
exercises.hint: Embedded question: no inversion — "where it comes from" (but "where the information comes from" = object noun clause)

exercises.text: "The editor couldn't decide ___ publish the unverified story before the deadline."
exercises.hint: "Couldn't decide whether to + infinitive" — no subject after "whether to"

exercises.instruction: Convert the direct question to an embedded form.
exercises.text: "Why does emotional content spread faster?" → She explained ___ emotional content ___ faster.
exercises.hint: Embedded: no auxiliary inversion — "why + S + V"

exercises.text: "The question of ___ media ownership affects reporting quality is well-established in research."
exercises.hint: "The question of whether" (yes/no) or "the question of how" (mechanism)

exercises.text: "Researchers investigated ___ bots were used to amplify the disinformation campaign."
"I wonder ___ social media companies are doing enough to prevent disinformation."
exercises.hint: "Wonder whether/if" — both acceptable in mid-sentence embedded yes/no questions

exercises.text: "She asked what did the fact-checker find."
opts: "Did the fact-checker find" should be "the fact-checker found"
exercises.correct: "Did the fact-checker find" should be "the fact-checker found"
exercises.hint: Embedded questions: no auxiliary inversion — "what the fact-checker found"

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct noun + wh-clause.
exercises.text: "The matter of ___ owns major news outlets affects ___ gets reported." (two wh-clauses)
exercises.hint: "Who + V" = the person who; "what + V" = the thing that

exercises.text: "___ the story reached so many people before being corrected remains unclear."
exercises.hint: "Whether + S + V" as a subject noun clause — "if" cannot begin a subject clause

exercises.text: "Who spread the disinformation?" → Researchers are trying to find out ___ the disinformation ___ (spread).
exercises.hint: "Find out + who + S + V" — no inversion

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form for a formal academic context.
exercises.text: "There is ongoing debate about ___ self-regulation by platforms is sufficient."
"Many doubt ___ governments have the political will to regulate AI-generated content." (= not sure if)
exercises.hint: "Doubt whether" — expressing uncertainty about a yes/no outcome

opts: I wonder where does misinformation originate.
I wonder where misinformation does originate.
exercises.hint: Embedded question: no auxiliary inversion — "where + S + V"

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct option for a formal written context.
exercises.text: "The issue of ___ to regulate AI-generated news has not yet been resolved." (choice of action, no new subject)
exercises.hint: "The issue of whether to + infinitive" = formal noun phrase + infinitive embedded clause

questions.text: "I wonder ___ the source of the story can be verified." (embedded yes/no question)
"The debate about ___ social media platforms should have editorial responsibility is ongoing."
"Can you explain ___ algorithms decide what content to show users?"
questions.hint: Embedded question: no inversion — "how + S + V"

questions.text: "She couldn't decide ___ trust the unverified account or wait for confirmation." (choice with infinitive)
"Researchers investigated ___ bots had been used to amplify the campaign."
"She asked what did the fact-checker find" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: No inversion in embedded questions: "what the fact-checker found"

questions.text: "The question of ___ AI-generated content should be labelled is increasingly urgent."
questions.hint: "The question of whether + S + V" = noun + embedded yes/no question

questions.text: "I don't know ___ the article is from." (source — wh-question)
questions.hint: "Know + where + S + V" — no inversion: "where the article is from"

questions.text: "Many doubt ___ platforms can effectively police their own content." (expressing uncertainty)
questions.hint: "Doubt whether" = uncertainty about a yes/no outcome

questions.text: "___ the disinformation campaign originated has never been officially established." (= where it came from — subject clause)
questions.hint: "Where + S + V" as a subject noun clause

questions.text: "Journalists need to find out ___ the account belongs to before publishing." (= who owns it)
questions.hint: "Find out + who + S + V" — no inversion

questions.text: Which sentence uses the noun clause correctly?
opts: "I wonder where does the story come from."
"I wonder where the story comes from."
"I wonder from where does the story come."
"I wonder that the story comes from."
questions.correct: "I wonder where the story comes from."
questions.hint: Embedded question: no inversion — "where + S + V"
